unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: Learning objective: Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design (Skill 1.A).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: Know that an experience is an event or occurrence, including interacting with actual surroundings, imagining abstract and fictional concepts, communication, and research; reflecting on experiences often sparks questions and inspires investigation, and experiences can be documented by recording observations and perceptions related to them.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: Know that documentation is recording information, in many formats including images (e.g., drawings, photos, diagrams, videos), samples of materials, models, verbal description, and sound; documentation of works can be shared with viewers to affect interpretation and feedback, furthering the artist's/designer's understanding of viewer responses.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: Know that viewers are people who look at a work of art or design, and that the artist or designer who made the work is also a viewer.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: Know that interpretation is understanding based on personal experiences and perspectives.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.A Document experiences to generate possibilities for making art and design. [Skill 1.A]
outcome: 1.A.5: Know that feedback is information about how someone responds to a work of art or design; it can be spontaneous and informal or more formal and structured, can be a conversation, written commentary, and/or nonverbal (e.g., a physical reaction; a response presented by drawing), and ideally is constructive (useful).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.B Document examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 1.B]
outcome: Learning objective: Document examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation through art and design (Skill 1.B).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.B Document examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 1.B]
outcome: Know that documentation of experiences becomes a resource for the artist/designer, can be shared with viewers, and can be presented as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.B Document examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 1.B]
outcome: Know that a sustained investigation through art and design is an inquiry-based, in-depth study of materials, processes, and ideas done over time that expands awareness of possibilities for making; investigation includes asking questions about materials, processes, and ideas within and beyond art and design, and a question (words used to find information) can be as simple as who, what, when, where, why, how, what if, and why not.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.B Document examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 1.B]
outcome: Know that sustained investigation is guided by questions or inquiry and involves research (discovering or verifying information); investigation includes perception, curiosity, examination, discovery, imagination, interpretation, description, and conversation, and can confirm and challenge thinking, revealing connections and opportunities.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Learning objective: Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design (Skill 1.D).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that researching investigations of artists, designers, and people working in other disciplines develops understanding of how inquiry guides the making of art and design; research can be indirect (e.g., examining how a designer's work shows evidence of inquiry) or direct (e.g., talking with a physicist about the questions they asked and how they investigated them).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that examples of how inquiry guides sustained investigation can be documented by recording questions, lines of inquiry, investigative processes (e.g., practice, experimentation, revision), and outcomes (e.g., learning about materials, processes, and ideas and asking more questions); documentation becomes a resource and can be shared with viewers, as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that interpretation of art and design can be investigated by describing the materials, processes, and ideas (components) of works, the context of works, and viewer responses to works.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that context is information about when, where, how, why, and by whom a work was made and viewed, and that context affects how a work is interpreted by its maker and by viewers.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that the materials, processes, and ideas used to make a work influence the artist or designer making it and influence viewer interpretations; people associate what they perceive in a work with their own experiences, affecting their interpretation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that by investigating how viewers interpret art and design based on materials, processes, and ideas, artists and designers develop understanding of how people respond to work, including their own, and learn about their own interpretations of art and design.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.C Document investigation of viewers' interpretations of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that investigations of viewer interpretation can be documented by recording questions, lines of inquiry, and investigative processes and outcomes (e.g., talking with viewers to learn how they interpret a specific material used in a sculpture); documentation becomes a resource and can be shared with viewers, as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.D Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions. [Skill 1.C]
outcome: Learning objective: Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions (Skill 1.C).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.D Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions. [Skill 1.C]
outcome: Know that artists and designers make work in the context of art and design traditions established throughout history by diverse cultures around the world; they are influenced by work they experience, and their work likely influences those who experience it.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.D Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions. [Skill 1.C]
outcome: Know that artists and designers can connect their work with traditions by comparing their materials, processes, and ideas with those of artists and designers in different contexts (from the artist working next to them to prehistoric cave painters); considering each work's context (when, where, how, why, and by whom it was made and viewed) lets works be related more appropriately, and comparing works reveals similarities and differences, often highlighting distinctive aspects of each.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.D Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions. [Skill 1.C]
outcome: Know that awareness of art and design traditions can expand possibilities for thinking and making; relating their work to traditions, artists and designers can decide whether to align with or challenge them, and documenting influences of traditions can demonstrate integrity by acknowledging references and influences.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.D Document how works of art and design relate to art and design traditions. [Skill 1.C]
outcome: Know that documentation of how works relate to art and design traditions becomes a resource, can be shared with viewers, and can be presented as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Learning objective: Document evaluation of art and design (Skill 1.D).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that works can be interpreted through evaluation, using evidence to compare work with specific criteria such as the artist's or designer's goals; AP 2-D Art and Design, AP 3-D Art and Design, and AP Drawing portfolios are evaluated on specific criteria in the scoring guidelines involving relationships (connections) of materials, processes, and ideas.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Evaluate works by: carefully and methodically observing the work and identifying its materials, processes, and ideas (components) individually, pointing out, listing and discussing them with visual evidence; focusing on one component and its visual connections to others (e.g., a material and a process and how they connect, then the ideas and whether the relationships are clear and strong and whether other viewers interpret them similarly); observing and reflecting on individual and combined effects of components; considering how connections could be strengthened to show synthesis (integration or coalescence of materials, processes, and ideas); identifying the use of specific skills (e.g., how color is skillfully used to emphasize shapes integral to a graphic design concept); and considering how visual evidence of the skills used could be strengthened.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that communication between the artist/designer and viewers can inform evaluation, and that evaluative decisions about relationships of materials, processes, and ideas, whether made by the artist/designer or a viewer, should be supported by visual evidence within the work.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that evaluation by considering relationships of materials, processes, and ideas may be spontaneous and informal, done by the artist or designer as they work, or more formal and structured, with feedback from peer reviews, group critique, a teacher, mentor, or client, and that it develops understanding of how components interact.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.E Document evaluation of art and design. [Skill 1.D]
outcome: Know that documentation of evaluation becomes a resource for the artist/designer, can be shared with viewers, and can be presented as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.F Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate. [Skill 1.E]
outcome: Learning objective: Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate (Skill 1.E).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.F Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate. [Skill 1.E]
outcome: Know that selecting materials, processes, and ideas may be intentional, based on experiences, interests, and availability of materials and tools; selection can be spontaneous (open to experimentation and discovery) or strategic (focused on a question, hypothesis, or goal), and considers inherent (observable, physical) and interpreted (determined by context, including personal and cultural perspectives of the artist/designer and viewers) attributes.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.F Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate. [Skill 1.E]
outcome: Know that investigating materials, processes, and ideas beyond those traditionally used to make art and design can expand possibilities for thinking and making, and that researching what diverse thinkers and makers use can inform selections.

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.F Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate. [Skill 1.E]
outcome: Know that selecting one component to investigate can lead to questions about the others, e.g. selecting a material leads to questions about processes (how can the material be used?) and ideas (what concepts and connotations are associated with it?).

unit: Big Idea 1: Investigate Materials, Processes, and Ideas
topic: 1.F Document selection of materials, processes, and ideas to investigate. [Skill 1.E]
outcome: Know that selections can be documented with images (e.g., drawings, photos, diagrams, videos); samples of materials, models, verbal identification, description, questions, and/or rationales; and/or sound; this documentation becomes a resource, can be shared with viewers, and can be presented as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.A Formulate questions or areas of inquiry that guide a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 2.A]
outcome: Learning objective: Formulate questions or areas of inquiry that guide a sustained investigation through art and design (Skill 2.A).

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.A Formulate questions or areas of inquiry that guide a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 2.A]
outcome: Know that a sustained investigation through art and design is an inquiry-based, in-depth study of materials, processes, and ideas done over time.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.A Formulate questions or areas of inquiry that guide a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 2.A]
outcome: Identify an inquiry for sustained investigation by: reflecting on documentation of experiences; thinking about past and current experiences and work, as well as knowledge, skills, intentions, and goals; inquiry about materials, processes, and ideas; open-ended queries beginning with what if, how, why; focusing on questions that can guide thinking and making; envisioning possibilities within and beyond art and design; organizing questions by grouping similar ones; evaluating and ranking questions by their potential for discovery; and exchanging constructive feedback about clarity and each other's questions' potential to inspire in-depth investigation over time.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.A Formulate questions or areas of inquiry that guide a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 2.A]
outcome: Know that questions are continually formulated, documented (visually and with writing), developed, and evaluated throughout a sustained investigation; investigation and making often inspire more questions, and learning and discovery can lead to refinement of questions.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Learning objective: Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry (Skill 2.B).

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that practice is repeatedly using a material, process, or idea over a period of time, and that practice should support learning and development.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that experimentation is testing a material, process, or idea; an experiment can begin with a question as simple as "What if . . . ?", involves trying something different, and can give surprising results that spark new ways of thinking about and using components.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that practice and experimentation often include revision to modify, clarify, or reimagine works and ideas; revision can be spontaneous, quick changes during the working process or methodical, complex, substantial changes after stopping to evaluate work, is often based on bringing together actual and desired states of work, and can include consideration of relationships of materials, processes, and ideas.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that practice, experimentation, and revision using materials, processes, and ideas can develop understanding of and skills using particular components; lead to refinement, distillation, elaboration, and discovery; and guide and further investigation, leading to discovery, transformation, and in-depth exploration.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that feedback on practice, experimentation, and revision can provide insight about the effects of those activities.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Conduct a sustained investigation by: formulating and selecting questions or areas of inquiry to guide practice, experimentation, and revision; selecting, practicing with, experimenting with, and revising materials, processes, and ideas in relation to the questions or areas of inquiry that guide investigation; documenting practice, experimentation, and revision in relation to guiding questions or inquiry; reflecting on relationships of questions and practice, experimentation, and revision; exchanging constructive feedback about visual evidence of sustained investigation in each other's work; and revising questions or areas of inquiry as a result of learning from practice, experimentation, and revision.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.B Conduct a sustained investigation through art and design that demonstrates practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 2.B]
outcome: Know that documentation of a sustained investigation should include visual evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision and of their effects, can also include written descriptions, becomes a resource for the artist/designer, and can be shared with viewers as a work and/or as part of a sustained investigation.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.C Make works of art and design that demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 2.C]
subtopic: Synthesis of materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Learning objective: Make works of art and design that demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas (Skill 2.C).

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.C Make works of art and design that demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 2.C]
subtopic: Synthesis of materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Know that the materials, processes, and ideas in a work may be visually unrelated or disconnected, related or connected, or synthesized, and that synthesis is demonstrated by visual evidence of integration or coalescence of these components.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.C Make works of art and design that demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 2.C]
subtopic: Synthesis of materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Make work showing visual evidence of synthesis (a goal of the AP 2-D Art and Design, AP 3-D Art and Design, and AP Drawing portfolios) by: selecting materials, processes, and ideas considering their individual and combined characteristics; identifying the components used, with visual evidence; considering each component's relationships with the others; making deliberate, clear, visual connections among them; practicing, experimenting, and revising combinations to strengthen relationships; describing how they are related, with visual evidence; and exchanging constructive feedback about clarity of relationships (e.g., moving from digital photography to an anthotype process with plant-based photosensitive materials to synthesize idea, material, and process in an investigation of negative human impacts on the environment).

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.D Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 2.D]
outcome: Learning objective: Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills (Skill 2.D).

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.D Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 2.D]
outcome: Apply 2-D skills, the two-dimensional elements and principles: point, line, shape, plane, layer, form, space, texture, color, value, opacity, transparency, time; unity, variety, rhythm, movement, proportion, scale, balance, emphasis, contrast, repetition, figure/ground relationship, connection, juxtaposition, hierarchy.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.D Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 2.D]
outcome: Apply 3-D skills, the three-dimensional elements and principles: point, line, shape, plane, layer, form, volume, mass, occupied/unoccupied space, texture, color, value, opacity, transparency, time; unity, variety, rhythm, movement, proportion, scale, balance, emphasis, contrast, repetition, connection, juxtaposition, hierarchy.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.D Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 2.D]
outcome: Apply drawing skills: mark-making, line, surface, space, light and shade, composition.

unit: Big Idea 2: Make Art and Design
topic: 2.D Make works of art and design that demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 2.D]
outcome: Make work showing visual evidence of skills (a goal of the AP 2-D Art and Design, AP 3-D Art and Design, and AP Drawing portfolios) by: selecting materials, processes, and ideas considering how skills will be developed and demonstrated using them; selecting specific skills to develop and demonstrate; developing specific skills through practice, experimentation, and revision; identifying and describing specific skills demonstrated within a work, with visual evidence; and exchanging constructive feedback about clarity of visual evidence of specific skills.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Learning objective: Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design (Skill 3.C).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Know that materials are physical substances used to make works of art and design, processes are physical and conceptual activities (including applications) involved in making them, and ideas are concepts used to make them.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: When identifying a work's materials, processes, and ideas in writing: begin by carefully and methodically observing the work; consider which components are used, and why and how; and use clear, concise words to give essential information about materials, processes, and ideas.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: When writing about materials, processes, and ideas, make strong connections between visual evidence in the work and the words used, avoiding visually obvious, less important information and focusing on more important, less visible aspects (e.g., a tree drawn with a charred twig on paper found on the ground: "burned twig on found paper" and "foraging, burning, recycling, and observational drawing" rather than "charcoal on paper" and "drawing").

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Know that researching artists' and designers' written descriptions of the components in their work can further develop writing skills, and that exchanging constructive feedback about clarity and effectiveness of writing about materials, ideas, and processes can hone writing.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.A Identify in writing, materials, processes, and ideas used to make works of art and design. [Skill 3.C]
subtopic: Writing about materials, processes and ideas
outcome: Know that written identification of materials, processes, and ideas used to make art and design is a form of documentation that becomes a resource for the artist/designer and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.B Describe how works of art and design demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 3.D]
outcome: Learning objective: Describe how works of art and design demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas (Skill 3.D).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.B Describe how works of art and design demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 3.D]
outcome: Know that describing synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas builds understanding of how components can coalesce or be integrated; investigating and analyzing interactions of components within diverse works informs learning about how synthesis can be achieved, and discussing relationships between components hones understanding of how synthesis is visually evidenced.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.B Describe how works of art and design demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 3.D]
outcome: To describe relationships among materials, processes, and ideas in a work: begin by carefully and methodically observing it, identifying components individually (pointing out, listing and discussing them); compare characteristics of one component with another, identifying similarities and differences; describe relationships among all three types of components, giving examples of visual evidence of their connections; and consider how visual evidence of connections could be strengthened to show synthesis (the effect of combined components being greater than the effect of individual ones).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.B Describe how works of art and design demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas. [Skill 3.D]
outcome: Know that description of how works demonstrate synthesis is a form of documentation that becomes a resource for the artist/designer and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.C Describe how works of art and design demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 3.E]
outcome: Learning objective: Describe how works of art and design demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills (Skill 3.E).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.C Describe how works of art and design demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 3.E]
outcome: Know that skills shown in a work can be pointed out, listed, and discussed, citing visual evidence from the work; describing 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills observed in diverse works builds understanding of how skills can be demonstrated, and discussing them hones understanding of how skills are visually evidenced.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.C Describe how works of art and design demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 3.E]
outcome: To describe how skills are demonstrated in a work: carefully and methodically observe the work, identifying a specific visually evident skill (e.g., describing how skillful use of color in a graphic design emphasizes shapes integral to the design concept); continue describing how other skills are shown; and consider how visual evidence of skills could be strengthened.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.C Describe how works of art and design demonstrate 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills. [Skill 3.E]
outcome: Know that describing how works demonstrate skills is a form of documentation that becomes a resource for the artist/designer and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.D Identify, in writing, questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 3.A]
outcome: Learning objective: Identify, in writing, questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation through art and design (Skill 3.A).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.D Identify, in writing, questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 3.A]
outcome: To identify in writing the questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation: reference documentation of questions or inquiry recorded throughout the work; reflect on the questions or inquiry initially formulated and how they changed; carefully and methodically observe the work made; use clear, concise words to identify the questions or inquiry; consider connections between the words and visual evidence in the work; communicate the inquiry that guided the work; and try different approaches to writing and evaluate their effectiveness in conveying the inquiry and aligning with the work within the portfolio.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.D Identify, in writing, questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 3.A]
outcome: Know that researching artists' and designers' written questions and descriptions of inquiry that guided their work can support development of writing skills, and that exchanging constructive feedback about clarity of written questions can hone writing.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.D Identify, in writing, questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation through art and design. [Skill 3.A]
outcome: Know that written identification of questions or inquiry that guided a sustained investigation is a form of documentation that becomes a resource for the artist/designer and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.E Describe, in writing, how a sustained investigation through art and design shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 3.B]
subtopic: Writing about practice, experimentation and revision
outcome: Learning objective: Describe, in writing, how a sustained investigation through art and design shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry (Skill 3.B).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.E Describe, in writing, how a sustained investigation through art and design shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 3.B]
subtopic: Writing about practice, experimentation and revision
outcome: To describe this in writing: make sure the guiding questions or areas of inquiry are clearly identified in writing; carefully and methodically observe the work within the sustained investigation; reference documentation of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry; use clear, concise words to describe those activities and how they were guided by questions or inquiry; consider connections between the words and visual evidence in the work; try different approaches to writing and evaluate their effectiveness; and consider writing about what was done, how it was done (practice, experimentation, and revision in relation to questions), and why (to conduct a sustained investigation).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.E Describe, in writing, how a sustained investigation through art and design shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 3.B]
subtopic: Writing about practice, experimentation and revision
outcome: Know that researching artists' and designers' writing about practice, experimentation, and revision can develop writing skills, and that exchanging constructive feedback about clarity of descriptions can hone writing.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.E Describe, in writing, how a sustained investigation through art and design shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry. [Skill 3.B]
subtopic: Writing about practice, experimentation and revision
outcome: Know that written description of how a sustained investigation shows evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision guided by questions or inquiry is a form of documentation that becomes a resource for the artist/designer and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
outcome: Learning objective: Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation (Skill 3.F).

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
outcome: Know that presenting works to viewers for interpretation involves deciding what to show, when, how, and to whom; different ways of presenting can lead to different interpretations (even for the maker), and the artist or designer has the power to affect how the materials, processes, and ideas within a work are perceived through decisions about how they present or display it.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
outcome: Know that work can be presented informally (e.g., showing work in progress and asking questions to elicit feedback about a specific component) or formally (e.g., showing a collection of completed works publicly to multiple viewers), and that presentation can include information about the work, such as documentation of materials, processes, and ideas, and communication between artist or designer and viewer.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
outcome: Know that showing work to viewers can build artists' and designers' understanding of how viewers interpret the materials, processes, and ideas used in a work, and can inform thinking and making.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
subtopic: Presenting the portfolio and documenting presentation
outcome: Know that when submitting an AP 2-D Art and Design, AP 3-D Art and Design, or AP Drawing Portfolio Exam, images and works must be presented so evaluators clearly see accurate representations of work and work processes: check lighting, focus, and overall clarity of each digital photograph for legibility, and carefully review the writing, which is part of the presentation, so it clearly conveys ideas in response to the prompts.

unit: Big Idea 3: Present Art and Design
topic: 3.F Document presentation of works of art and design for viewer interpretation. [Skill 3.F]
subtopic: Presenting the portfolio and documenting presentation
outcome: Know that presentation can be documented by recording information, based on direct observation, about what was shown and why, how, and to whom; documentation can include viewer interpretations of the work presented, becomes a resource for the artist/designer, and can be shared with viewers.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Know that all three AP Art and Design Portfolio Exams (AP 2-D Art and Design, AP 3-D Art and Design, AP Drawing) have two required sections, Selected Works (40% of total score) and Sustained Investigation (60%), scored separately and combined into an overall portfolio score; works may be made in art classes or on the student's own time and over more than one school year.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Selected Works: submit five digital images of five works that each demonstrate synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas using 2-D art and design skills (AP 2-D) or drawing skills (AP Drawing), or, for AP 3-D, 10 digital images consisting of two views each of five works using 3-D art and design skills.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: For each Selected Works piece, state in writing: idea(s) visually evident (250 characters maximum, including spaces), materials used (150), processes used (250), image citation (200) and digital tools (200); responses are evaluated with the images and are not evaluated for spelling, grammar, or punctuation.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Know that the five Selected Works are evaluated collectively and holistically on three criteria: works demonstrating 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills (Skill 2.D), works demonstrating synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas (Skill 2.C), and identifying in writing materials, processes, and ideas used (Skill 3.C).

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Know that any material, process, idea, style, or content is acceptable as long as work is the student's original creation; any use of preexisting source material, including imagery generated by tools or systems, must be cited and observably transformed through the student's own practice, experimentation, and revision.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Sustained Investigation: submit 15 digital images of works of art and process documentation that demonstrate sustained investigation through practice, experimentation, and revision; sustained investigation of materials, processes, and ideas; synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas; and 2-D/3-D/drawing skills (depending on portfolio type), united by a single guiding inquiry.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: State in writing (850 characters maximum each, including spaces): the inquiry that guided the sustained investigation and how tools, research, and experimentation (including digital or AI-assisted ideation, if applicable) developed and refined it; and the ways the investigation developed through practice, experimentation, and revision, including any use of digital tools or AI and how reflection and decision-making guided them, emphasizing authorship and ethical use.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: For each Sustained Investigation image, identify materials used (150 characters maximum), processes used (350), digital tools (200), size (height × width × depth, in inches; "N/A" allowed for process or detail images; intended display size for digital work) and image citation (200), citing any pre-existing source material and showing how it was transformed.

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Know that the 15 images are evaluated collectively on four separately scored criteria: formulating and identifying in writing guiding questions or inquiry (Skills 2.A and 3.A, 20%); written and visual evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision (Skills 2.B and 3.B, 30%); synthesis of materials, processes, and ideas (Skill 2.C, 30%); and 2-D, 3-D, or drawing skills (Skill 2.D, 20%).

unit: Portfolio Exam
topic: Portfolio Exam Structure
outcome: Document thinking and making throughout the sustained investigation with images and words, select process documentation and detail images that best show practice, experimentation, revision and synthesis, and sequence the images (no required order) to best demonstrate the investigation in relation to the written information.
